READABILITY.evidence: The code itself is clear: `if queryset.query.is_sliced: raise ValueError(...)`. But the error message ("Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken.") is reused at construction time, which hides why it's raised. The diff also adds stray blank lines in the code and docs.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: This bans a use case the issue asks to support instead of adding it. It puts a restriction in Prefetch.__init__ that blocks the feature, which makes future support harder. It also edits existing tests and documents the limitation as permanent. None of the existing ORM building blocks (Window, RowNumber) are reused.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: The validation turns a valid user request into a hard error rather than handling it. Sliced Prefetch querysets now fail earlier instead of working. All 4 F2P tests fail (PrefetchLimitTests).

C8-01-CASE1.evidence: No per-parent slicing at all. Prefetch.__init__ raises ValueError for any sliced queryset, so neither qs[n:] nor qs[n:m] works and Window/RowNumber is never used. F2P 0/4.
